title: Coherent shifts of the native strict Roos functor
statement: Let A be an abelian category with countable products, S a category with coherent integer shifts, and K:S→(ℕᵒᵖ→CochainComplex(A,ℤ)) a functor. Write F_n(X)=K(X)_n and τ_n:F_(n+1)→F_n for its transitions. Suppose every F_n has a coherent shift comparison and every τ_n commutes with these comparisons. The native strict Roos functor R(X)=Cone(1-s:∏_n F_n(X)→∏_n F_n(X))[-1] of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] has a coherent shift comparison. With the product comparison of [lem-weil-product-comm-shift], its two mapping-cocone inclusions have coefficients 1 and (-1)^m as in [lem-weil-signed-mapping-cocone-shift]. If a natural map b:T→R has zero second coordinate, and a map a:T(X[m])→T(X)[m] commutes with the first coordinate of b and the product shift, then a followed by b_X[m] equals b_(X[m]) followed by this native Roos shift.

proof.text: The pointwise level evaluations and tower transitions are functorial. Form their product functor and use the coherent product shift. Its projection formula fixes the chosen product comparison. Tower evaluation and adjacent transitions are defined over the underlying target category, so specializing them preserves the existing complex structure without inserting an abelian-instance conversion.

proof.text: The native transition endomorphism has nth projection pr_n minus pr_(n+1) followed by τ_n. Apply shifted projections to its shift square. The product projection formula and the assumed transition squares identify both sides.

proof.text: Over the arbitrary abelian category A, the native Roos functor is the signed mapping-cocone functor of this endomorphism. Use the signed cocone CommShift and its inclusion formulas. Its zero and addition laws give the required coherent native shift. This constructs the comparison before any coefficient specialization. Package the two coordinate equations as ConeFormula; replacing its product isomorphism by an equal prescribed comparison gives commShift_formula without re-elaborating the expanded coefficient-specialized cone.

proof.text: A map with zero second coordinate factors degreewise through the first cocone inclusion, by the mapping-cocone identity decomposition. Replace both sides of the proposed chain equation by these factorizations. The first-coordinate hypothesis and coefficient-one inclusion formula give equality degreewise, hence equality of chain maps.
